newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan securities chief optimistic about stocks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan securities chief optimistic about stocks.

text.p: The head of Taiwan's securities watchdog said on Tuesday he was optimistic about the island's stock market as the influence of non-economic factors were diminishing.
"I believe the market will have a rosy future. I am optimistic," Lu Tung-ying, chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission, was quoted as saying by his aide.
Local investors had become more rational in recent years and economic fundamentals would dominate the market's movements in the future, Lu's said, according to the aide.

The aide told Reuters that Lu said non-economic factors would have smaller impacts on the island's stock market, which had survived from plunges in 1990 and 1991 and China's intimidatory war games near Taiwan in March 1996.

Taiwan and China have been rivals since a civil war separated them in 1949. Beijing held missile tests near the island in the run-up to Taipei's presidential poll in March, triggering massive sell-off in the island's sensitive stock market.
However, the stock market was again hit by non-economic factors after Taiwan provincial governor James Soong resiged last month.
Soong, a ruling Nationalist Party heavyweight, resigned after refusing to accept an all-party decision to freeze provincial-level elections.
The index plunged 1.64 percent on Saturday as nervous investors worried that Soong's resignation would cause political instability.
The market rebounded on Monday and Tuesday and brokers said gains might be fuelled by the entry of government-related fund to support the market in the face of political uncertainty.
But analysts also said signs of a domestic economic recovery helped the rebound.

The Finance Ministry said on Tuesday that Taiwan's 1996 trade surplus jumped 81.3 percent from 1995 to US$14.704 billion and it projected the island's imports and exports both to rise by over eight percent in 1997.

"Expecting Taiwan's 1997 exports to rise more than eight percent is reasonable as the global trade is seen to grow some seven percent compared with 5.5 percent in 1996," said Daniel Chen, chief economist at ChinaTrust Commercial Bank.
On Tuesday, the index ended up 30.27 points or 0.44 percent to 6,875.02, off a 6,897.39 high. Turnover was an active T$50.61 billion.
